response_text: To pass an argument into a thread, the user first writes the thread function to take a void* argument and passes in their desired data (like a pointer to a struct or integer) when creating the thread. On the OS side, when the thread is being initialized, it sets up the stack for the new thread and manually places that argument in register R0, which is how the ARM Cortex-M architecture expects the first argument to be passed into a function. The OS also sets the PC to point to the thread function and sets the PSP to the top of the new thread's stack. This setup tricks the processor into thinking it's just calling a regular function with an argument, so when the thread starts running, it grabs the value from R0 and uses it as intended. This works because the whole process mimics the normal calling convention at the hardware level, so the thread behaves like a standard function call with a passed-in argument.\n
